title: stash-merge: KV-prefix reuse and delayed-dequant commit for mixed-precision continuous-batching
author: Asha Ramesh
description: Motivation: quantized inference on bursty, short-sequence traffic suffers from repeated dequant/requant work and KV-cache churn when continuous-batching mixes tokens from different requests. This PR implements a lightweight ‘stash-and-merge’ prefix reuse mechanism combined with per-layer scale pooling and a delayed-dequant commit to reduce redundant dequant ops during windowed KV reuse. Summary of changes: 1) Add a KV prefix stash that keeps lightweight compressed representations of recently evicted KV windows to allow immediate rehydration without full dequantization when the runtime detects high prefix reuse probability. 2) Introduce per-layer scale pooling metadata produced at model load time (scale_pool.json blobs) so INT8/FP8 layers share quantization scaling when safe, reducing per-token recompute of rescale factors in the fast path. 3) Implement a delayed-dequant commit point in the continuous-batching pipeline: dequant work is staged and only committed for tokens that are about to be shipped to the network or to layers that require full-precision inputs, enabling amortized dequant when tokens are later merged from stash. 4) Kernel/runtime: small refactor of int8_microkernel and fp8_fuse paths to expose a dequant hint API and a compact in-memory stash format. 5) Heuristics: per-customer and per-route knobs (default-on for hosted) to control stash size, stash TTL, and the confidence threshold for reuse. 6) Extensive test harness and benchmarks (bench/stash_merge/) covering end-to-end latency, p50/p95/p99, and memory overhead. Performance: in internal benchmarks on a 48GB A100 pool with a real-world bursty chat workload, we observe 18-32% improvement in token throughput for short sequences (1-32 tokens) at p95 tail latency kept within 5% of baseline. Memory overhead for stash (default config) is ~3-6% at 500 qps; CPU amortization reduces per-token dequant CPU by ~27%. Backwards compatibility: stash format is versioned; when disabled by config the runtime falls back to current KV eviction+rehydration path. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to canary hosts (10%) for two weeks, metrics guarded (token throughput, dequant CPU, KV rehydrate latency), followed by progressive ramp to 100% with an automatic rollback if p95 latency regresses >10%. Security & privacy: stash entries are kept in-process and respect existing KMS/encryption boundaries in private deployments; no new network surface added. Risks & mitigations: potential correctness edge-cases for poorly calibrated per-layer pools—added regression suite with golden prompt sets and a validation job that compares outputs against baseline float32 to detect regressions >0.5% token-level divergence. Related work: builds on prior KV-windowing, dequant-fusion and hybrid-quant scheduling efforts (see ENG-281, ENG-303). Implementation notes: added config flags: runtime.kv.stash_enabled, runtime.kv.stash_ttl_ms, quant.scale_pool_path, runtime.dequant.delayed_commit_threshold. Documentation & examples: updated docs/ops/kv-stash.md and examples/quickstarts/stash_tuning.ipynb. Owner: Asha Ramesh. Impact: notable improvement for chat/assistant workloads where prefix reuse is common, minimal risk to long-sequence throughput.

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: overall this looks promising. Can you clarify memory accounting for stash entries under low-memory nodes? I’d prefer an LRU with strict budget enforcement.
Asha Ramesh: added strict budget enforcement and low-memory fallback to immediate eviction; updated tests to simulate OOM conditions.
Priya Patel: CI showed a flaky test in bench harness on p95 measurement after the first commit; re-run and ensure determinism.
Asha Ramesh: fixed timing nondeterminism by seeding the harness RNG and added retries in CI job; re-ran benchmarks and attached stable numbers.
Ethan Liu: can we expose a diagnostic metric for stash hit-rate per-route and integrate into console? Also add a SLO guard to prevent stash-induced p99 regressions.
Asha Ramesh: added runtime.metrics.kv_stash_hit_rate and a p99 guard metric; console dashboard patch will follow in a separate PR (docs ticket ENG-3622).

Release notes: Adds KV prefix stash and delayed-dequant commit to reduce redundant dequant work; improves short-sequence token throughput by up to 32% under bursty traffic. Config flags available to opt out.
release_notes: Adds KV prefix stash (stash-and-merge) and delayed-dequant commit to amortize dequantCost in mixed-precision paths; default-on for hosted; knobs available for tuning; benchmarks show 18-32% throughput win for short sequences.
notes_for_cherry_pick: Small change to third_party/format/v1/stash_schema.proto required a compatibility guard when cherry-picking to release-1.4. Backported with schema v1->v1beta compatibility layer.
test_instructions: Run ./ci/bench-stash-merge.yml on a 48GB GPU instance with bench/stash_merge/bench_driver.py using workload config workloads/chat_bursty.yaml. Validate metrics: runtime.metrics.kv_stash_hit_rate > 0.05 and dequant_cpu_pct decreases by ~25%.
observability_changes: Added runtime.metrics.kv_stash_hit_rate, runtime.metrics.kv_stash_rehydrate_latency_ms, runtime.metrics.quant_scale_pool_miss_rate. Dashboard panel templates under docs/ops/kv-stash.md.
changelog_entry: Feature: KV stash + delayed dequant commit (stash-merge) to improve short-sequence quantized inference throughput. Opt-out via runtime.kv.stash_enabled=false.
security_notes: Stash entries remain in-process and are cleared on eviction; keys and sensitive payloads are not serialized outside the process. For Private deployments, stash respects existing KMS/HSM boundaries.
